keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Mombasa as an independent Mazrui sultanate, 1746-1837. The page gives the town, never a boundary or an area; the radius is the size of the hole Cliopatria cuts at Mombasa in its 1824-1827 Omani shape (10 cells). The British protectorate (1824-1826) and the Omani liwalis (1826-1837) are carried by the ledger.

region.text: Mombasa Island and its mainland; the pages name no Mazrui land beyond the town

ledger.note: 1746: the Mazrui make Mombasa independent of Oman. 'Four new Omani Liwali until 1746, when the last of them made it independent again (disputed by Oman)'; 'Ali ibn Uthman al-Mazru'i is the first sultan of the list (1746-1755). The Fort Jesus page puts the start of local rule in 1741.

region.text: Mombasa Island and its mainland; the pages name no Mazrui land beyond the town

ledger.note: 9 February 1824: Mombasa becomes a British protectorate. 'From 9 February 1824 to 25 July 1826, there was a British protectorate over Mombasa, represented by governors' (infobox: British Empire 1824-1826); the sultan of the list, Sulayman ibn 'Ali, reigns 1823-1826.

region.text: Mombasa Island and its mainland; the pages name no Mazrui land beyond the town

ledger.note: 25 July 1826: the protectorate ends. The British protectorate ran 'to 25 July 1826'; 'Omani rule was restored in 1826; seven liwalis where appointed'. The Omani dossier draws the liwalis' Mombasa as a vassal from this date.

25 July 1826: with the end of the British protectorate Mombasa comes under Omani suzerainty. Mombasa page: 'Omani rule was restored in 1826; seven liwalis where appointed' (infobox 'Sultanate of Zanzibar 1826-1887'); the Fort Jesus page keeps local rule until 1837, so the relation is a vassal tint until the annexation of 24 June 1837. [Reviewer af-05, 2026-10-19: added as the mirror of the omani-slave-coast vassal_start of July 1826.]

ledger.note: 24 June 1837: Said bin Sultan annexes Mombasa. 'On 24 June 1837, it was nominally annexed by Said bin Sultan of Muscat and Oman'; the Fort Jesus page: 'The fort fell under local rule from 1741 to 1837... when it was again captured by the Omanis and used as a barracks'.

wars.name: Battle of Shela
wars.outcome: Failure: 'The attempt failed totally, and many were killed'; Pate, allied with the Mazrui clan, had tried to subject Lamu and did not.
wars.note: 'In 1813, the famous Battle of Shela took place at Shela.' The page's 'Mazrui clan from Mombasa/Oman' leaves open whether the Mazrui sultan took part as a state. No border moved.

sources.note: Mombasa history: Portuguese 1593-1698, 1631 revolt, 1698 Omani capture, Mazrui independence 1746, British protectorate 1824-1826, annexation by Said 24 June 1837, 1887 relinquished to the British East Africa Association, 1895.

sources.title: Fort Jesus
sources.note: Fort built 1593-1596; Sultan Yusuf ibn al-Hasan took it in 1631, Portuguese back 1632; Omani siege 1696-1698; Portuguese again 1728-1729; local rule 1741-1837; Omani capture 1837.

notes:
New state: Cliopatria has no Mombasa row. This dossier covers only the Mazrui sultanate (1746-1837). The Mombasa page also gives the earlier city-state, not drawn here: a Sultan of Mombasa before 1300, part of the Kilwa Sultanate 1300-1513 (infobox) though 'In 1502, the sultanate became independent from Kilwa Kisiwani' (text), the Portuguese under Almeida in 1505, the city destroyed in 1528 by Nuno da Cunha, the Ottoman admiral 'Ali Bey in 1585 (infobox 1586-1589), the Portuguese takeover 'a third time in 1589' and Fort Jesus 1593 (see portuguese-mombasa), Omani liwalis from 1698. A gap-filler could add a 'Sultanate of Mombasa (Swahili era)' dossier from those lines.

Disagreements: independence 1746 (Mombasa page) or 1741 (Fort Jesus page); after 25 July 1826 the Mombasa page has Omani rule restored with seven liwalis and its infobox Zanzibar rule to 1887, while the Fort Jesus and Said bin Sultan pages have local (Mazrui) rule until Said's capture in 1837. The dossier ends the sultanate on 24 June 1837 and the Omani dossier carries the 1826-1837 vassal tint.

The Mazrui article opened (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazrui) is a clan article with no dates; it adds that the Mazrui opposed the Al Bu Sa'id and attacked Stone Town at least once, undated. No page opened gives the Mazrui lands outside Mombasa (Takaungu, Gazi, Vanga, Pemba): not recorded.

Counterparts needing dossiers: british-colonial-empire (eu-11; 1824-1826 protectorate, vassal_start with this state as counterpart), sultanate-of-oman (me-10), pate-sultanate and Lamu (Lamu is not a dossier here).
